title: Ben Kedirah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Tosefta Gittin 2:11: Rabbi Yehudah said, “It happened with Ben Kedirah that he used to write blank forms of bills of divorce בערב [in Arav, or: in the evening].” Zuckermandel’s Tosefta reads Ben Karara.

notes.text: בערב can denote “in the evening” or the place Arav. The saved Machon Mamre digital Tosefta Gittin 2:11 repeats the same word and does not itself settle the sense. Both possibilities remain visible; no place identity or time-of-day is asserted as settled.

Zuckermandel’s printed Tosefta gives Ben Karara at the end of Gittin 2:10 (pp. 325–326), where the story runs over the page break. The Machon Mamre text places the story at 2:11 and gives Ben Kedirah. Both write בערב without vowels. Samuel Klein understood it as the Galilean town Arav. The two texts give different details about Rabbi Elazar’s exceptions, and the spelling alone leaves the place and time readings open.
